This is confirmed and cross-checked from two independent Node.js documentation fetches plus a search across multiple version pages of the official docs, so I'm treating both facts as verified.

## 1. `4 % 2` per the ECMAScript specification

**Result: `0`**

The `%` operator invokes the `Number::remainder(numerator, denominator)` abstract operation (ECMA-262, §6.1.6.1.6, Numeric Types — Number). For non-zero, finite operands the spec defines the result as `r := n - d × q`, where `q` is the integer nearest zero with the same sign as `n` such that the relation holds. With `n = 4, d = 2`: `q = 2`, so `r = 4 - (2 × 2) = 0`.

- Primary source: [ECMAScript® 2027 Language Specification — Numeric Types §6.1.6.1.6, `Number::remainder`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-numeric-types-number-remainder) (tc39.es, live/current draft spec).
- Corroborating source with a worked example matching the spec algorithm verbatim: [MDN — Remainder (%)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Remainder), which lists `4 % 2; // 0` explicitly.

## 2. Minimum Node.js version for the built-in `node:test` module

This project's `package.json` test script is `"test": "node --test"`, i.e., it invokes Node's built-in test runner (`node:test`).

**Minimum version: Node.js `v16.17.0`** (first backport), with the mainline introduction at **`v18.0.0`**. It only became API-stable (Stability 2) as of **`v20.0.0`**; before that it was experimental.

- Source: [Node.js API docs — Test runner (`node:test`)](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html), whose History section states the module was "Added in: v18.0.0, v16.17.0" and "The test runner is now stable" as of v20.0.0. This same History note is present verbatim on the v20.x, v21.x, v22.x, and v24.x documentation pages I checked, confirming it's a stable, cross-version fact rather than a one-off doc error.

**Practical takeaway:** if this project's CI/dev environment needs `node --test` to run at all, Node ≥ 16.17.0 is the hard floor (experimental); if it needs the stable, non-experimental API, Node ≥ 20.0.0 is the safe minimum to target.

### Not independently verified
- I could not get a raw-HTML confirmation of the exact `Number::remainder` algorithm text directly from tc39.es (the fetch tool returned only a table-of-contents excerpt on two attempts); the algorithm text above is corroborated via a search-engine excerpt of the same tc39.es page plus MDN's matching transcription, not a direct page scrape I performed myself.

Sources:
- [ECMAScript® 2027 Language Specification — Number::remainder](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-numeric-types-number-remainder)
- [MDN — Remainder (%)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Remainder)
- [Node.js v26.x API docs — Test runner](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html)
- [Node.js v20.x API docs — Test runner](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v20.x/api/test.html)
